claim: Let \(k=\mathbb F_q\) and \(L=ke\oplus kf\) with \([e,f]=f\). Every 2-local automorphism \(\Phi:L\to L\) is uniquely determined by a permutation \(\sigma\) of \(k\) and a scalar \(\kappa\in k^\times\), via \(\Phi(ae+bf)=ae+a\sigma(b/a)f\) for \(a\ne0\) and \(\Phi(bf)=\kappa bf\) on the line \(a=0\). Consequently there are exactly \(q!(q-1)\) such maps, of which \(q(q-1)\) are automorphisms, and every 2-local automorphism is an automorphism if and only if \(q=2\).
integrity: The proof is symbolic and covers all finite fields; no finite computation is used as proof. Self-review only; independent audit and independent validation have not been performed.
scientific_limitations: The classification is for the two-dimensional nonabelian Lie algebra over finite fields only.
The proof uses finiteness to turn an injective slope map into a permutation.
No classification is claimed for infinite fields or higher-dimensional solvable Lie algebras.
title: Exact classification of 2-local automorphisms of the finite-field affine Lie algebra
